name: ola
desc: Open Lighting Architecture for lighting control information
why: Open Lighting Architecture speaks DMX and Art-Net, a door into stage lighting protocols that few developers ever touch.

brief.what_it_is: OLA (Open Lighting Architecture) is a lighting-control package, described in the formula as Open Lighting Architecture for lighting control information. The Homebrew formula installs a daemon, olad, plus a set of command-line tools whose names suggest DMX512 output, RDM device discovery and configuration, Art-Net and E1.31 (sACN) network input and output, USB DMX interfaces, timecode, and a recorder. I did not read the README or docs, so these functions are inferred from executable names, not confirmed. The scout note frames it as a door into stage lighting protocols that few developers touch.
brief.why_it_exists: The scout note says it gives developers access to stage lighting protocols such as DMX and Art-Net. I could not confirm the author's own framing because the README did not load.
brief.install_notes: Homebrew's caveat says Python support has been removed, citing https://github.com/OpenLightingProject/ola/issues/2008. Anyone expecting Python bindings should check that issue first. I did not find other setup, hardware, or first-run steps because the README did not load.
brief.standout: Per the scout note, OLA exposes DMX and Art-Net, which are rarely approached by general software developers. The executable list shows a full toolkit (RDM discovery and set/get, USB Pro firmware, a stream client, a DMX monitor and console) rather than a single utility.
brief.status: unknown. I got no release date, last commit, or README statement. The homepage returned HTTP 500, and the GitHub README fetches returned only the bare word 'README'.
brief.caveats: The homepage returned HTTP 500, so the project's own description was not read. Both GitHub fetches returned only the string 'README' with no content, so no README text, commands, or quotes were verified. Python support was removed according to the Homebrew caveat. License, platform support, and build requirements are unchecked. The what_it_is and standout fields rely on the formula description, the executable names, and the scout note, not on the project's documentation.
